goal: Remove contract-to-implementation reverse dependencies without changing v1 wire or persisted shapes.

capability.strategy: Move the closed literal union to the contract owner; make the runtime CAPABILITIES vocabulary satisfy that contract while retaining runtime validation in src/domain/capabilities.ts.
acceptance: CAPABILITIES remains the runtime vocabulary/validator owner
no new compatibility alias is added

resource-limits.strategy: Declare the structural ResourceLimits contract in host.ts. Keep RESOURCE_FIELDS and validation runtime-owned, with the descriptor checked against every contract key.
acceptance: RESOURCE_FIELDS remains the executable range/unit owner
contract and runtime descriptor keys are compile-time exhaustive

protocol-limits.strategy: Declare the structural ProtocolLimits contract in host.ts. Keep PROTOCOL_LIMIT_FIELDS and validation runtime-owned, with the descriptor checked against every contract key.
acceptance: PROTOCOL_LIMIT_FIELDS remains the executable range/unit owner
contract and runtime descriptor keys are compile-time exhaustive

transaction-port.strategy: Replace the concrete Store Transaction alias with a contract-owned transaction port covering only methods consumed across module boundaries; make src/store.ts structurally conform. Do this last because it has the widest internal surface.
acceptance: the contract exposes no sqlite or concrete storage implementation type
module conformance proves the Store transaction implementation satisfies the port

guardrails: Do not move runtime validators/defaults/effectful descriptors into implementation/contracts.
Do not change public wire fields, durable JSON, error codes, or crash ordering as part of this cleanup.
Do not replace one reverse dependency with another src/* type import from contracts.
